thread:
noah-finance: Quick one  partner reseller applied promotional credits at checkout for EU customer via our marketplace. Partner asks us to gross-up their payout to cover VAT they will owe locally. Who signs off and what's the VAT treatment on the invoice we issued to the end-customer?

sara-tax: Two separate issues: 1) VAT on the sale to the end-customer: depends on whether sale is B2B or B2C and the place of supply rules. If the end-customer is B2B with valid VAT ID and supply is cross-border, reverse charge may apply and we (or partner, depending on marketplace model) shouldn't charge VAT. If B2C, VAT should be charged at customer's location. 2) Partner payout/gross-up is a commercial decision between Redwood and partner, not a VAT rule per se, but VAT on the partner's services may arise locally for them.

lucas-partner-ops: Clarify marketplace flow: Redwood invoices the end-customer and pays partner a share, or partner invoices their revenue share to Redwood? Right now we invoice end-customer and settle partner via a revenue share credit. Partner says they will owe VAT on their share and want a gross-up.

paula-sales: Usually partner is responsible for their own VAT. If they want us to increase payout, budget owner must approve. But we also need to know if Redwood should have charged VAT on the end-customer invoice in the first place.

acct-pay: Practical: for reissues/credit notes we need original invoice number, partner ID, customer's VAT ID (if B2B), evidence (VIES screenshot), and partner VAT registration proof. Also tag FIN-6175 if we proceed.

ledger-bot: Invoice generated: INV-2027-2104 for acct EU-RETAIL-9. Link: https://billing.redwood/invoices/INV-2027-2104

sara-tax: Action items: 1) Determine who is the supplier of record for VAT: Redwood (marketplace principal) or partner (agent). If partner is principal and collects from end-customer, partner should account for VAT. If Redwood is principal, Redwood accounts for VAT and can reclaim/offset where appropriate. Check reseller contract. 2) If Redwood charged VAT incorrectly on a B2B sale where reverse charge applies, issue credit note + reissue with reverse-charge statement and include customer's validated VAT ID. 3) For partner gross-up requests: treat as commercial concession. If approved, document as a one-off commissioning fee with invoice annex and update the payout schedule. Include VAT on the gross-up if that payment is subject to VAT locally.

noah-finance: Contract says partner is an "approved reseller (agent)" but ambiguous. I'll attach the reseller agreement clause and mark for legal to confirm principal vs agent.

paula-sales: Customer is a small Irish startup and provided VAT ID: IE3456789A. We currently charged 23% VAT on the invoice because checklist defaulted to B2C.

sara-tax: If IE3456789A validates in VIES and is indeed a company, it should be B2B reverse charge. We should issue credit note + new invoice without VAT, include phrase: "Reverse charge  customer liable (Article 196)" and customer's VAT ID. Keep note: "Promo credits applied as discount" in invoice narrative. Attach VIES screenshot.

lucas-partner-ops: Partner asks for gross-up of 23% on their payout share to cover their VAT liability. If we increase payout, do we pay VAT on that increased amount as well?

sara-tax: If the gross-up payment is treated as consideration for a service Redwood receives (i.e., a fee), then any VAT due depends on where the supplier (partner) is established and place of supply. For simplicity: treat the gross-up as a separate line item on the settlement memo labelled "partner gross-up (tax reimbursement)". It may be subject to local VAT for partner; Redwood shouldn't self-charge VAT on a payout to partner. But partners must invoice Redwood if they require VAT to be charged. Consult Legal on how to document.

acct-pay: To process any adjusted payout we need: partner VAT number, partner invoice for gross-up (if they issue one), settlement memo, and budget owner approval. Creating FIN-6175 now.

noah-finance: Proposed steps: 1) Run VIES check on customer's VAT ID and attach screenshot. 2) Legal to confirm reseller principal/agent. 3) If reverse charge valid, issue credit note + reissue invoice. 4) Partner to submit a formal request for gross-up with calculation and their VAT invoice if applicable. 5) Finance to route gross-up to budget owner for signoff.

paula-sales: I'll validate VAT ID and upload screenshot. Customer prefers reissue rather than refund.

sara-tax: Also engineering ask: log marketplace role (agent/principal) and VAT IDs in billing metadata so future automated VAT routing is possible. And store VIES responses for audit.

lucas-partner-ops: I'll reach out to partner for formal gross-up request and request their VAT registration cert.

acct-pay: FIN-6175 created. Will await attachments.

noah-finance: Thanks all. One more: invoice preview after promo credits looked like this:

```
- list_price: 1,200.00 EUR
- promo_discount: -200.00 EUR
- net: 1,000.00 EUR
- VAT 23%: 230.00 EUR  <-- currently charged but may be removed with reissue
```

noah-finance: Any objections to the proposed flow?

paula-sales: No objections. We'll proceed once VIES and legal confirmation are in.

sara-tax: Agreed. Keep all docs in FIN-6175 and tag tax reviewer when ready.
